# Overview

This report is generated automatically by the daily **Ebola Analytics
Pipeline**. It shares its data, parameters, prediction zones, and
coefficients with the interactive portal at the repository root.

The workflow below follows a stepwise SIR modelling cycle:

1. Data preparation
2. Data wrangling
3. Computation of primary parameters from the raw data
4. Model generation (training)
5. Model testing (holdout)
6. Model performance analysis
7. Projection (14 days)

The population at risk is fixed at **`r format(N_total, big.mark = ",")`** persons,
consistent with the portal.

# STEP 1 — Data Preparation

```{r step1}
knitr::kable(head(raw, 5), caption = "Raw upstream series (head)")
cat("\nRows:", nrow(raw), " Columns:", ncol(raw), "\n")
cat("Columns:", paste(names(raw), collapse = ", "), "\n")
```

# STEP 2 — Data Wrangling

```{r step2}
knitr::kable(
  head(outbreak_df[, c("date","suspected","confirmed","total",
                       "deaths","recovered","active_cases","cfr")], 8),
  caption = "Cleaned series with derived active cases and CFR"
)

cat("\nClean rows:", nrow(outbreak_df),
    "  Range:", as.character(min(outbreak_df$date)),
    "→", as.character(max(outbreak_df$date)), "\n")
```

# STEP 3 — Primary Parameters Computed from Raw Data

```{r step3}
param_table <- data.frame(
  Parameter = c(
    "Population at risk (N)",
    "Initial susceptible (S₀)",
    "Initial infectious (I₀)",
    "Growth rate (r)",
    "Recovery rate (γ)",
    "Mortality rate (μ)",
    "Transmission rate (β = r + γ + μ)",
    "Basic reproduction number (R₀ = β / (γ + μ))"
  ),
  Value = c(
    format(N_total, big.mark = ","),
    format(round(S0), big.mark = ","),
    format(round(I0), big.mark = ","),
    sprintf("%.4f /day", growth_rate),
    sprintf("%.4f /day", gamma_est),
    sprintf("%.4f /day", mu_est),
    sprintf("%.4f /day", beta_est),
    sprintf("%.3f",       R0_est)
  )
)
knitr::kable(param_table, caption = "Primary parameters derived from raw observations")
```

**Key calculations**

- Growth rate: log-linear regression on the first 30 % of the **daily
  incidence** series, using the model ``log(I(t)) = a + r·t``.
- Recovery rate: ``γ = 1 / 10 days`` (mean infectious period).
- Mortality rate: ``μ = (CFR / 100) / infectious period``, giving a
  **daily** hazard out of the I compartment.
- Transmission rate: closed-form from the SIR early-phase identity
  ``r = β − γ − μ``, so ``β = r + γ + μ``.
- Basic reproduction number: ``R₀ = β / (γ + μ)``.

# STEP 4 — Model Generation (Training Set)

```{r step4}
knitr::kable(
  head(as.data.frame(sir_train), 6),
  caption = "Trained SIR compartments — first six days"
)
cat("\nTraining window:", train_n, "days  (",
    sprintf("%.0f%%", TRAIN_FRACTION * 100), "of observations)\n")
```

# STEP 5 — Model Testing (Holdout Set)

```{r step5}
test_df <- data.frame(
  Day       = full_times[test_mask],
  Observed  = observed_I[test_mask],
  Predicted = round(predicted_I[test_mask], 0),
  Residual  = round(observed_I[test_mask] - predicted_I[test_mask], 0)
)
knitr::kable(test_df, caption = "Holdout window — observed vs predicted")
cat("\nHoldout window:", test_n, "days\n")
```

# STEP 6 — Model Performance

```{r step6}
perf_tbl <- data.frame(
  Window  = c("Train", "Test", "Overall"),
  RMSE    = round(c(train_perf$rmse, test_perf$rmse, overall$rmse), 2),
  MAE     = round(c(train_perf$mae,  test_perf$mae,  overall$mae),  2),
  R2      = round(c(train_perf$r2,   test_perf$r2,   overall$r2),   3)
)
knitr::kable(perf_tbl, caption = "SIR model performance metrics")

cat("\nInterpretation notes:\n")
cat("- RMSE and MAE are in units of cumulative cases.\n")
cat("- R² closer to 1 indicates better explanatory power.\n")
cat("- Negative R² indicates the model performs worse than the mean.\n")
```

# SIR Compartments with β, γ, μ Reference Lines

```{r sir-compartments, fig.height=6}
sir_long <- sir_full %>%
  select(time, S, I, R, D) %>%
  pivot_longer(-time, names_to = "compartment", values_to = "value")

# Scale parameters to the I compartment for visual reference
# (they are daily rates, so we plot them on a separate scale — here
# we annotate them as horizontal dotted lines with right-edge labels).
param_lines <- data.frame(
  rate  = c(beta_est, gamma_est, mu_est),
  label = c(sprintf("β = %.3f", beta_est),
            sprintf("γ = %.3f", gamma_est),
            sprintf("μ = %.3f", mu_est)),
  col   = c("#c0392b", "#27ae60", "#8e44ad")
)

# For the plot, we draw the compartment curves on the left axis and
# the parameter values as scaled dotted lines so they remain visible.
scale_factor <- max(sir_long$value, na.rm = TRUE) /
                max(param_lines$rate, na.rm = TRUE) * 0.35

ggplot(sir_long, aes(x = time, y = value, colour = compartment)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.1) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = param_lines$rate * scale_factor,
             linetype = "dotted", colour = param_lines$col,
             linewidth = 0.8) +
  annotate("text",
           x = max(sir_long$time) * 0.98,
           y = param_lines$rate * scale_factor,
           label = param_lines$label,
           hjust = 1, vjust = -0.4,
           colour = param_lines$col, size = 3.3, fontface = "bold") +
  labs(x = "Days since first report",
       y = "Individuals (compartments) / scaled rates (dotted)",
       title = "SIR compartments with β, γ, μ reference lines",
       colour = "Compartment") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(legend.position = "right")
```

# 14-Day Projection

```{r projection}
proj_df <- as.data.frame(sir_proj)
knitr::kable(head(proj_df, 15),
             caption = "14-day SIR projection (next two weeks)")
```

```{r projection-plot, fig.height=5}
proj_long <- proj_df %>%
  select(time, S, I, R, D) %>%
  pivot_longer(-time, names_to = "compartment", values_to = "value")

ggplot(proj_long, aes(x = time, y = value, colour = compartment)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.2) +
  labs(x = "Days since first report",
       y = "Individuals",
       title = "Projection of SIR compartments over the next 14 days",
       colour = "Compartment") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(legend.position = "right")
```
